How Much of This Backtest Is Credible?

A backtest's Sharpe ratio is an estimate, and one that was usually picked as the best of many attempts. This report measures the uncertainty of that estimate, discounts it for the number of variants tried, and checks whether the edge survives out-of-sample and over time.

Findings

  • warning OUT_OF_SAMPLE_DEGRADATIONSharpe fell from 0.74 in-sample to -0.45 out-of-sample (p=0.042).
  • warning OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SHARPE_NOT_POSITIVEOut-of-sample Sharpe is -0.45.
  • warning PROBABILITY_OF_BACKTEST_OVERFITTINGPBO is 72.7%: in that share of train/test splits the best in-sample variant ranked in the bottom half out-of-sample.
  • caution SHARPE_NOT_SIGNIFICANT_AFTER_SELECTIONDeflated Sharpe is 64.5%: after accounting for 60 trial(s) there is less than 95% confidence that the true Sharpe is positive.
  • caution TRACK_RECORD_TOO_SHORTAbout 49,314 observations are needed to confirm this Sharpe at 95%; the sample has 2,520.
  • caution SHARPE_CI_INCLUDES_ZEROThe 95% bootstrap interval for the annualised Sharpe is [-0.24, 1.06], which includes zero.
  • caution ALPHA_NOT_SIGNIFICANTAlpha of 5.14%/year has a t-statistic of 1.91; performance is not distinguishable from benchmark exposure (beta 0.49).
  • info FAT_TAILSSkew 0.92, kurtosis 12.4: Sharpe hides tail risk here; read it together with drawdown and the Montecarlo report.

Sharpe Ratio Significance

The probabilistic Sharpe ratio is the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero given sample length, skew and fat tails. The deflated Sharpe ratio raises the bar to the best Sharpe expected from 60 skill-less trial(s). The minimum track record is the number of observations needed for the observed Sharpe to be significant.

Alpha and Alpha Decay

Alpha is the return left after removing benchmark exposure (r = α + β·benchmark). The dashed line is a linear time trend fitted to the full sample with Newey–West standard errors: a significantly negative slope means the edge is decaying.

Probability of Backtest Overfitting

Combinatorially symmetric cross-validation: the history is cut into blocks, every half/half combination is used as train/test, and each time the best variant in-sample is ranked out-of-sample. PBO is the share of splits where that winner lands in the bottom half.
